question.problem: A seed packing company claims that the germination rate of the seeds is $75%.$ What is the probability that exactly $3$ seeds will germinate from $5$ seeds selected at random? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of seeds that will germinate.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=5$ seeds

- the probability of the germination of the seeds is $p=75%=0.75$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(5,0.75).$ We want to find the probability that exactly $3$ seeds will germinate.

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=3) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{3})(0.75)^{3}(1-0.75)^{5-3} \\  & =\frac{5!}{3!(5-3)!}(0.75)^{3}(0.25)^{2} \\  & =10(0.75)^{3}(0.25)^{2} \\  & ≈0.264\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
